comment: The revert-checks of `tooling-portability` (labels 5.1–5.7) and of `fix-portability-value-set-and-preconditions` (labels 6.1–6.5), plus the fixture's missing budget default (7.1), as a runnable set: one mutation each, the named case must go red, the file is restored, the case must go green again. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/portability-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how, `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule. The evidence recorded in the change's `evidence/` came from exactly these mutations.

mutations.why: the value set is read from the profile, not hard-coded
the source adapter is excluded from the engine set
the profile is resolved from the working tree, not from $HOME

mutations.label: 5.3b
mutations.why: …and a linked worktree resolves its own profile, not one read from $HOME (the same mutation, the task's second case)
GITHUB_REPOSITORY does not override the working tree
the synthetic project's repository differs from this one
the prompt substitutes the project's gate command instead of owning one
every command in the porting recipe runs
every namespace's value set is read and forbidden, not the category's alone

mutations.replace: : # the submodule path is not read from the loop's configuration
mutations.why: the submodule path is read from loop.conf, not named in the engine
the reserved label is asserted as the one read-only exception, not tolerated
the suite refuses when its root is not a git working tree
the suite refuses when its root is machine-local state
a budget default the engine reads is declared by the fixture's configuration, not left to the host's (issue #290)
